title: Last night's data source: IPMA's own messages, found through MeteoAlarm, published as cap.json
span: 10 to 11 November, 21:23 to 08:26 UTC. Our reading of which source Dinis meant, to be confirmed by him
summary: **Our reading, to be confirmed by Dinis:** neither the storyteller nor the conductor can place his words ("an agent needing a data source, then a researcher finding out, and then the website published a JSON file, and then I came along") with certainty; this is the best candidate in the record, the conductor's and ours. At 21:23 on Tuesday IPMA moved Lisbon's red rain warning to 09:00; the open-data feed the site read did not show it for about two and a half hours. The meteorologist found IPMA's own messages (CAP), with their send times, in MeteoAlarm's public feed; the conductor published them as cap.json at 23:53. Within ten minutes the weather watch checked MeteoAlarm's terms and found what was missing; the meteorologist added the link and disclaimer; the designer put MeteoAlarm's line in every page's footer. By morning cap.json was what the front page and the timeline read first. Where Dinis "came along" is not in the record we hold: that step is left open until he says.

In the other repository; the conductor reports the meteorologist's commit there as 169445f, 23:52

steps.before: the night and the morning: cap.json is read on every sync

pauses_note: The pause that matters is the first: two and a half hours in which the warning existed and the site's feed did not have it. After the source was found the rest took ten minutes. Dinis's own step ("and then I came along") is not drawn: it has no time in the record we hold, and it waits for his word.
shows: A data source arrives because an agent notices a gap (two of IPMA's channels disagree), finds where the body's own words are published, and the site publishes them as a JSON with their read time, for people and agents alike.
A new source brings its terms with it: within eight minutes another agent checked them, and within ten the link and disclaimer were on every page. Licence is part of the data.
The find outlived the night: cap.json is what made the morning's wind downgrade (path 6) a fact on the site 22 minutes after IPMA sent it, while the open-data feed lagged again.
reading: This path is labelled as our reading because Dinis's words name roles ("an agent", "a researcher") that fit two agents here: the meteorologist found the feed and the researcher read IPMA's send times from it an hour later. The conductor has asked Dinis; when he answers, this page will follow him.

Two of the hashes (169445f, d6ce188) are in the Web Summit site's repository, which this session cannot read; they are given as the conductor reported them. Every other step rests on a commit in this repository.
